Casio · ref. PRW-61

Protrek

Outdoor/Field · c. 45–58mm · 100–200m · quartz

The Pro Trek is Casio's line of outdoor watches, defined by its sensor technology for navigating the wilderness. Signature features include a built-in digital compass, barometer, altimeter, and thermometer, collectively known as the "Triple Sensor" or, in later models, "Quad Sensor" with the addition of a step tracker.

The story

Introduced in the mid-1990s, the Pro Trek family began with the groundbreaking "Triple Sensor" technology, offering climbers and hikers crucial environmental data on their wrists. The line evolved with key technological upgrades, including the addition of Tough Solar charging in the early 2000s to reduce the need for battery changes during expeditions. Later, the integration of radio-controlled timekeeping, known as Multi-Band 6, ensured atomic accuracy. Over the years, Casio has focused on making the watches more compact and introducing analog-digital displays, while consistently improving the precision and efficiency of its sensors.

References by era

ATC-11001994
The first Casio watch with Triple Sensor technology, a precursor to the Pro Trek line.
DPX-5001995
The first model to officially carry the Pro Trek name, establishing the brand's identity.
PRT-40c. 1996
An early model featuring an auto EL backlight. The PRT-410 owned by members is from this era.
PRG-402000
Featured a large dual-layer LCD for improved compass readability and an altimeter that could measure up to 10,000 meters.
PRW-10002005
The first Pro Trek to incorporate both Tough Solar power and radio-controlled timekeeping.
PRW-60002014
An analog-digital combination model equipped with the more advanced Triple Sensor Version 3 and Smart Access crown.
PRT-B502019
Introduced Quad Sensor technology, adding a step counter, and Bluetooth connectivity for linking with a smartphone.
PRW-612022
A recent model notable for its use of bio-based resins in the case and band, reflecting a focus on sustainability.
